3. On the aforesaid First Information Report the police visited the place of occurrence, recorded statement of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and prepared a sketch map with index, too the victim to the Upazila Magistrate for recording statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and after completion of investigation submitted charge sheet. The accused-appellant with his wife said Anu Begum alias Anwara Begum were put on trial under sections 376/114 of the Penal Code under the Special Powers Act before the learned Additional Sessions cum Special Tribunal Judge, Jamalpur in the aforesaid case. The accused pleaded not guilty to the charge and claimed to be tried. 

 5. The prosecution examined 10(ten) witnesses in the case and on closing of the evidence the appellant and his wife were examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to which they pleaded not guilty and declined to adduce any evidence. 

 6. On consideration of the evidence on record, the trial Court acquitted co-accused Anu Begum ali as Anwara Begum of the aforesaid charges and convicted the appellant under section 376 of the Penal Code and sentenced him as aforesaid. The appellant then preferred this appeal against the said order of conviction and sentence. 

 Mr Sultan Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the convict-appellant, submits that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment and the order of conviction and sentence is not maintainable in view of the evidence on record and the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside. He further submits that the First Information Report was lodged 10 days after 00-15 hour of the night of 10-11-89 without medical examination of the victim girl and the evidence of PWs suffer from serious omission and contradictions. He also submits that the prosecution having failed to prove their case beyond doubt, the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside. In support or his submission the learned Advocate has referred a decision in the case between Akhter Hossain and others vs State, reported in 4 BLC 236 and another in the case between Abdul Wahed alias Chandu Mia vs State reported in 4 BLC 320. The learned Advocate further submitted that the learned Additional Sessions Judge has passed the impugned judgment without proper assessment of evidence of the PWs and, as such the said judgment is not maintainable in law. He refers a decision in the case between Abu Taher Chowdhury vs State reported in 42 DLR (AD) 253 in support of his submission. 

 21. PW 1 Mr MA Rashid, the Investigating Officer, has stated in his examination-in-chief that he was attached to Jamalpur Police Station on 10-11-89 when informant Shamsul Haque lodged the First Information Report under sections 376/114 of the Penal Code on which Jamalpur PS Case No.4 dated 10-11-89 was started. He took up the charge of investigation, visited the place of occurrence, prepared sketch. map with index, recorded statements of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, prepared seizure-list, sent the victim to the Court for recording her statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, took step for her medical examination and after investigation submitted charge-sheet against the appellant and his wife Anwara Begum @ Anu on 31-12-89 under sections 376/114 read with section 9 of the Nari Nirjatan Ain. In his cross- examination this PW stated with reference to houses marked 'A' that 'Gha' and 'Cha' marked houses in the sketch-map belonging to Tofazzal and Nur Uddin are within the close vicinity of the place of occurrence marked 'A' but none of the inmates of those houses has been examined in the case as witness. He also stated that he did not examine Asmat Ali, Jamiruddin, Marfat, Aziz, Ratan, Hiron, Hekrnat, Kalu and Delwar and has not cited any of them as witness. This PW also stated in his cross that he did not seize any wearing clothes of the victim. This PW stated further that, none of the witnesses has stated to him that accused's daughter Hena took the victim girl to their house on the date of occurrence. He also stated that PW Motaleb did not tell him that accused Shamsul Hoque violated the victim girl for two consecutive nights. 

 22. On perusal of the evidence of the PWs it appears that the PW 1 lodged the First Information Report on 10-11-89 alleging the aforesaid occurrence mentioning the age of his victim daughter as 9 years. But while deposing he mentioned the age of the daughter as 11 years in his examination-in-chief PW 1 lodged the First Information Report on 10-11-89 alleging that the occurrence took place on 1-11-89 and 2-11-89, that the victim girl was brought back to his house by her friend Hena and Hena's mother accused Anwara Begum @ Anu on 3-11-89. PW 1 explained the delay saying about a local salish. But none of the PWs particularly PWs 1-5 gave any date of holding of the salish in their deposition. PW1 also stated in his chief that, while his victim daughter wanted to return home she was resisted by the accused, that accused Anu took away Hena after his daughter fell asleep, that the accused-persons requested his daughter not to divulge the incident to anybody, that Sanwara had blood-stain on her pant and that she narrated the incident to him and other witnesses, have not been mentioned in the First Information Report lodged by him 10 days after the occurrence. The statement made in his examination-in-chief by the PW 1 that accused Anu took away Hena after his daughter had fallen sleep or that Sanwara had blood-stained pant has not been corroborated by PW 2 the victim girl herself and by other PWs as well. PW 1 mentioned the names of Kalu, Tara, Jalil, Rahim, Hiron, Mizan, Suruj and others in the First Information Report stating that her daughter narrated the incident to them. But none of them has been examined as a witness in the case. The PW 1 also mentioned in the First Information Report that he lodged the First Information Report on 10-11-89 after medical treatment of his daughter which caused delay in lodging the First Information Report But from the evidence of PW 8 Dr Md Hatem Ali, Civil Surgeon of Jamalpur General Hospital it appears that the victim Sanwara Begum was examined by him on 12-11-89 and her X-ray was taken on the same date and the X-ray report was signed on 14-11-89. It also appears from the evidence of PW 1 that he was working in the restaurant of one Habu in Jamalpur Railway Station and he raised an unauthorised Chhapra Ghar in the Railway Colony and used to live there with his step-daughter along with others. Although this PW had denied the defence suggestion that due to unsocial activities of his daughter the hut was demolished by the local people, but he admitted that he does not live in the said hut which he allegedly sold away. It is not clear that how an illegal occupant can sell his hut raised unauthorisedly in the Railway land. It also appears from the deposition of PW 1 in cross that Asmat AIi, Seman, Jamiruddin, Marfat, Aziz, Ratan, Hiron, Hekmat, Jadu, Kalu, Delwar and others who lived there surrounding the hut of the informant have not been examined in the case. It also appears from cross- examination that, Jamila Khatun, mother of the accused Anu, was a Railway maid and she lived near the house of the informant and Hena used to live with her in the same house. The evidence of PWs 8 and 9 show that the PW 2 was produced before them on 12-11-89 and 11-11-89 respectively which belies the examination of delay in 10 days in lodging the First Information Report on 10-11-89 at 00.15 hrs. It is also mysterious and remained unexplained as to why the First Information Report was lodged 10 days after at about 'zero' hour of 10-11-89 at 00.15 hours. 

 24. PW 3 has stated in his cross that he heard the victim girl narrating the incident to others. It appears from his evidence that he did not hear the victim girl personally. He stated in cross that there were about 15 persons in the salish including Commissioner Didarul Alam, Ex-Chairman Moyenuddin Mondal, Rahmat, Motaleb informant, Matiur Rahman, Danesh Uddin, Chairman and others but except Didarul Alam and Motaleb none has been examined in the case. PW 4 Didarul Alam has also deposed in his chief that he does not remember the name of the victim girl and that he heard the incident 7/8 months before from the informant. He stated in his cross examination that there are 10/12 persons in the salish but none of them heard the victim girl. PW 5 Md Abdul Motaleb admitted in his cross-examination that the Investigating Officer did not examine him. 

 25. PWs 1-5 spoke about the salish but none of them has given the date of salish. PW 3 stated in cross that there were 15 persons in the salish, on the other hand PW 4 stated that there were 10/12 persons in the salish. They mentioned names of a number of local leading personalities but were not examined in the case. From their evidence it appears that the prosecution has failed to prove that any salish was held as alleged on the alleged occurrence. PW 8 Dr Md Hatem Ali categorically stated in his deposition as well as in his X-ray report that the victim girl was aged 12 years, ill developed and her secondary sex character was not yet developed, on the other hand, the PW 1 gave the age of his victim daughter as 9(nine) years in the First Information Report and 11 years in his deposition. PW 8 further stated in his examination-in-chief that no extra genital injuries or signs of violation was detected after his careful examination, though he found the hymen was ruptured with rounded margin, but as the victim was produced after 10 days of the incident, no definite opinion could be given in respect of rape. In cross PW 8 stated clearly that no signs or marks of violence was found and that the hymen could be ruptured if the hymen falls on a foreign body or hard substance. The evidence of this witness however, does not at all prove that PW 2 was violated. PW 9, the Magistrate who recorded the statement of victim girl under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure stated in his cross-examination that, the victim did not state in her statement to him that she was violated on the next night by the accused. The PW 10 the Investigating Officer has named a dozen of persons living around the house close to the hut of PW 1 as marked in his sketch map but none of them was examined in the case as a witness. This PW also stated that he did not seize the wearing clothes of the victim girl. There is also no evidence on record in the case that the wearing clothes of the victim was sent for chemical examination. This PW 10 also stated in cross that no witness stated to him that Hena took the victim girl to their house and that accused Shamsul Hoque violated the victim for consecutive two nights. 

 26. From the above evidence it is difficult to draw a clear conclusion of violation of the victim girl by the accused-appellant Shamsul Hoque on the date, place and in the manner as alleged by the prosecution. The evidence of PW 2 Sanwara Begum the victim girl herself shows that, she was taken by her friend Hena to their house arid after night meal she slept on the floor of the room along with Hena and on the Chowki slept the parents of Hena in the same room. From the evidence we find presence of Hena up to the time of sleeping of the victim girl on the floor but she was found mysteriously absent and disappeared during the time of alleged occurrence and even on the next day and on the second night of repetition, till bringing her back to her hut. But a self-developed concocted story was introduced by PW 1 while deposing (in his chief) in the case that, Hena was taken away by her mother Anu after Sanwara fell into sleep. The PW 2 the victim girl has neither stated the same nor corroborated such statement of PW 1. The story of violation of PW 2by the accused-appellant for the consecutive two nights has also not been corroborated nor stated by the victim herself before the Magistrate in her statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It is highly unlikely and unnatural that a father will violate the minor friend of his own minor daughter with the help of the mother of their daughter. Even if we take it as nothing is impossible in the present day but the situation, facts, evidence and circumstances of the case do neither corroborate such a fact nor lead us to draw a definite conclusion on the happenings of such occurrence. 

 27. In such case the evidence of the victim girl is most important to believe or to disbelieve the occurrence even in absence of corroboration. But in the present case the prosecutrix herself has contradicted her own testimony in such major particulars that the story of her violation becomes unbelievable. The record shows that the police has admittedly not seized the wearing clothes of the victim girl as alamat and the same was not sent for chemical examination, although her father PW 1 deposed that her pant was blood-stained, The evidence on records further shows that although the First Information Report was lodged on 10-11-89, the victim was sent to the doctor (PW S) 10/12 days after the occurrence. She was also sent to PW 9 the Magistrate for recording her statement under section 164 of the CrPC 11 days after the occurrence. The medical evidence and opinion of PW 8 Dr Md Hatem Ali clearly says that no opinion of rape could be given in the situation of the case. 

 28. We agree with the decisions referred to by Mr Sultan Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the convict-appellant in the case between Akhter Hossain and others vs State, reported in 4 BLC 236 and another case in between Abdul Walled alias Chandu Mia vs State, reported in the same BLC 320, that this is a settled principle that in case of carnal offence the prosecution is to be believed in awarding conviction to the offender even without material corroboration, if her evidence is found otherwise believable and trustworthy and does not suffer from any infirmity and inherent disqualification. But we find in the present case the contradictions are so major as stated above the evidence of the prosecution cannot be believed. Moreover, her non-examination by the doctor immediately after the alleged occurrence and non- examination of her apparels chemically must be considered as vital omissions for a case of this nature which made the testimony of the victim unworthy to believe. The evidence of PWs 1 and 2 has not been corroborated by any independent witness as regards her going to the house of the accused-appellant and on other circumstance. It also appears that the age of the victim girl has been put in different place as 9, 10 and 12 years according to the sweet will of the prosecution. Admittedly, Hena, the friend of the victim girl and the leading personalities living around the house of the informant and of the appellant, were not examined. The mystery of lodging First Information Report at about 'zero' hours of 10-11-89 remained unexplained. 

 30. in view of the aforesaid facts, circumstances and evidence and in view of the omissions and contradictions in the evidence of the PWs particularly of PW 2, the victim girl herself, and in view of the evidence of PW 8 Dr Md Hatem Ali, as discussed above, we are unable to agree with the findings of and the order of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court. We also find that the trial Court has not assessed the evidence properly and we find it unsafe to convict the accused appellant on the evidence on record as quoted and discussed above. We are, therefore, of the opinion that the appeal must succeed and the order of conviction and sentence is liable to be set aside.
